text: Archaeological survey, Babylon 1750 BCE: Construction workers unearthed foundation stone inscribed Renovated 1750 BCE Original built 1750 BCE. Stone shows no signs of prior construction. Building exists in continuous present tense.

Medical records, St. Bartholomew's Hospital 1348: Patient admitted with plague symptoms recovers after consuming bread that won't be invented until 1928. Baker's apprentice claims recipe came to him in dreams of white coats and sterile room

Weather station logs, Nome Alaska 1952: Temperature recorded as 40F while thermometer simultaneously displayed 98F. Both readings accurate. Station operator reported feeling both frostbite and heat stroke within same hour.

Botanical survey, Amazon Basin 1889: Specimen collected exhibits reverse photosynthesis, converting oxygen to carbon dioxide in daylight. Plant thrives. Local guides report grove has existed since before trees learned to breathe properly.

Personal diary, Prague 1592: Woman documents daily conversations with her reflection. Reflection responds with different opinions, remembers events that never occurred. Mirror was installed facing blank wall.

Municipal census, Detroit 1973: Household counted 47 residents living in twobedroom apartment. Inspector confirmed accurate headcount. Building permits show structure physically accommodates maximum of 6 occupants.

Excavation report, Babylon 2100 BCE: Cuneiform tablet inventory lists 847 scrolls in library. Physical count yields 847 empty shelves. Scribes continue daily cataloging of invisible collection. Reading room remains fully occupied.

Blood test results, Stockholm 1967: Patient's blood type documented as AB during morning draw, O during afternoon draw. Same patient, same day. Both samples genetically identical. Patient required both universal donor and universal recipien

Shipping manifest, Port of London 1843: Vessel Mary Catherine recorded delivering cargo of winter to July. Harbor master notes summer temperatures dropped 23 degrees upon docking. Ship's hold contained crystallized August.

Paleontological survey, Morrison Formation: Stegosaurus skeleton, 155 million BCE, discovered wearing fitted bronze armor. Metallurgy predates earliest copper working by 154,990,000 years. Armor shows battle damage.

Weather station logs, Nome Alaska 1951: Barometric pressure readings recorded in iambic pentameter for entire month of February. Meteorologist's notes written in standard prose. Storm predictions achieved 97 accuracy.
Census records, Pompeii 78 CE: Population listed as 20,000 living residents, 3,847 not yet born. Vesuvius erupted the following year. All unborn citizens found in ash, fully formed.
Library circulation records, Alexandria 48 BCE: Final checkout before the fire was A Complete History of the Library of Alexandria by Marcus Didius. Book was due back in 52 BCE. Never returned.

Medical records, St. Bartholomew's Hospital 1665: Patient admitted with memories of plague he hasn't caught yet. Symptoms manifested three days before exposure. Recovery preceded infection by a fortnight.

Entry 1347A: Highway overpass constructed 1978 casts shadow of Roman aqueduct. Shadow functions as water channel during August thunderstorms. Engineering reports classify structure as functionally impossible, hydrologically sound.
